## Summary

- Most common failure type: production detail-route behavior not fully covered by wrapper tests and loaded-state-only visual review.
- Most frequently affected agents: `Pixel`, `Sentinel`, `Executor`, and `Orchestrator`.
- Highest-value improvement: production-route coverage for chrome/dock changes, plus route-state UI checks for loading, error, empty/not-found, and loaded states.
- MCP servers recommended: none. Local logs, tests, analyzer, custom lint, and code scans were sufficient.
- New agents recommended: none.

## 1. Rule Gaps

### RG-1: Detail-route chrome redesigns must cover every route state

Proof:

- `docs/LOG/SESSION_OpenDesign_DetailSurfaces_2026-05-21.md:19-21` records loaded-state-only chrome review gaps: loading route escape, async compact-dock shifts, and missing booking title identity after AppBar removal.
- `docs/LOG/SESSION_OpenDesign_DetailSurfaces_2026-05-21.md:31-35` records the applied fixes for loading back controls, tab height/offset, reserved report guard space, and booking identity surface.

Merged rule:

- `Pixel.md`: added a detail-route chrome/dock redesign rule requiring loading, error, empty/not-found, and loaded-state audits; visible escape affordance; in-content identity/title surface; stable tab height; stable async guard dock layout; tooltip and touch-target coverage for icon-only actions.

### RG-2: Wrapper tests can hide production chrome and action regressions

Proof:

- `docs/LOG/SESSION_OpenDesign_DetailSurfaces_2026-05-21.md:22-23` records that work and booking tests used wrapper copies with old AppBars and that icon-only action coverage was incomplete.
- `docs/LOG/SESSION_OpenDesign_DetailSurfaces_2026-05-21.md:38-41` records the production-route tests added for work, booking, and direct-offer report actions.

Merged rules:

- `Executor.md`: added a UI runtime test gate requiring production-route or production-route-body tests whenever route chrome, tabs, or bottom bars are replaced.
- `Sentinel.md`: added an approval gate requiring production coverage for route chrome/dock redesigns; wrapper copies may remain only as supplemental content tests.
- `Orchestrator.md`: added Master Report disclosure for whether route chrome/dock tests cover production routes or only wrappers.

## 2. Rule Clarity Gaps

- Existing visual-proof rules already said Open Design screenshots are not Flutter runtime proof. This pass did not duplicate that rule.
- Existing wrapper-test rules already required production theme/provider harnesses when wrappers consume app theme extensions. This pass adds the missing production-route coverage requirement for chrome, tabs, docks, and icon-only action priority.
- Existing behavior-level test rules already required testing runtime behavior after review fixes. This pass names the recurring detail-route surfaces where wrapper-only tests are insufficient.

## 3. MCP Recommendations

None.

The failure mode was not missing live access. It was an agent-rule gap around route-state review and test harness selection.

## 4. Missing Skills

The existing UI, hardening, architecture, and testing skills are sufficient. The missing piece was routing the lesson into the owning agents.

## 5. Agent Coordination Gaps

- `Pixel -> Sentinel`: Pixel must hand off all detail-route states and compact-dock stability expectations, not only the loaded-state composition. Sentinel must verify those behaviors in production-route tests or mark the gap open.
- `Executor -> Sentinel`: Executor must add production-route coverage when it keeps wrapper tests for Supabase-safe content rendering.
- `Sentinel -> Orchestrator`: Sentinel findings about wrapper-only coverage must appear in the Master Report instead of being hidden behind aggregate test success.

## 6. Orchestrator Pipeline Improvements

Master Reports now need to state whether route chrome/dock tests hit the production route/body or only local wrappers. Wrapper-only coverage is a remaining QA gap for chrome, tab, dock, tooltip, and action-priority behavior.
